subject.title: fix(telegram): wire spooledUpdateHandlerTimeoutMs config to polling session

question: Should OpenClaw expose `spooledUpdateHandlerTimeoutMs` as a supported per-channel and per-account Telegram configuration contract, rather than retaining only the existing environment-variable override?
rationale: The patch is more than an internal wiring repair: it defines a new user-facing, persisted configuration surface whose scope and precedence will become upgrade and support contract.

options.title: Sponsor the configuration field
options.body: Accept the channel/account configuration contract, then require a rebase and runtime proof that configured and unset fallback behavior both work.

options.title: Keep environment-only control
options.body: Decline the new config surface and document the supported environment override if it remains the intended operator control.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the configuration field
recommendation.body: Accept the channel/account configuration contract, then require a rebase and runtime proof that configured and unset fallback behavior both work.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only source-connected contributor identified in the supplied review data; a current-main Telegram configuration owner could not be attributed from the available evidence.
